e53194ec5f1b977c: KUALA LUMPUR: The Communications Ministry, through the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas), will study the residual payment or revenue-sharing mechanism for audiovisual works in Malaysia.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the study would take into account three main aspects, namely legislation, the structure of the creative industry ecosystem and current business models, and the practices of streaming platforms and international distributors.
"The study will examine whether the mechanism should be implemented through amendments to existing laws, industry guidelines or standard contracts," he said in a parliamentary written reply today.
He was responding to Kalam Salan (PN-Sabak Bernam) on whether the government planned to introduce a residual payment or rerun royalty mechanism for Malaysian actors.
Fahmi said Finas would work with the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Intellectual Property Corporation of Malaysia.
He said the mechanism could ensure actors continued to receive reasonable economic benefits when works featuring their performances were commercially exploited after their initial release.
He said this included through television reruns, streaming platforms and international markets.
Fahmi said the Copyright Act 1987 currently provided certain rights to performers.
"However, there is currently no specific mechanism for residual payments for audiovisual works.
"Actors' remuneration is generally determined based on the terms and conditions agreed between the actors and producers or rights holders," he said.

Fahmi said the views of stakeholders would also be taken into account, including the Federation of Malaysian Film Industry Workers Associations, actors' associations and producers' associations, to ensure the proposed mechanism considered the interests of all parties.
48fc8698c1bf7dbf: KUALA LUMPUR: A former bank officer was fined RM36,000 by the Sessions Court today on six charges of failing to report receiving more than RM80,000 in bribes for personal loan financing.
Judge Rosli Ahmad imposed the sentence on Noor Iskandar Aziz, 45, and ordered him to serve six months' imprisonment if he failed to settle the fine.

According to the alternative charges, Iskandar was accused of receiving six cash deposits, totalling over RM80,000, into accounts belonging to himself and his wife, from two individuals and a company, CSA Infinite Consultancy.

The gratification was for assisting the personal loan financing applications of customers of CSA Academy Sdn Bhd at a bank, concurrently with the personal loan applications of customers at several other financial institutions.
The accused, however, failed to report the gratification to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) or a police officer.

The offences were committed at two banks in Kuala Lumpur and Setia Alam between Oct 5, 2021 and May 11, 2023, under Section 25(1) of the MACC Act 2009 and punishable under Section 25(2) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum fine of RM100,000 or imprisonment for a maximum of 10 years, or both.
Deputy public prosecutor Irna Julieza Maaras urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence to serve the accused and the community a lesson.
Counsel Sean Dudley, appearing for the accused, pleaded for a fine only, on the ground that his client, who works as a delivery rider, supports his wife and two children.

"The accused suffers from hypertension, which requires continuous treatment and medication. He has also extended full cooperation to the MACC throughout the investigation, and has no previous criminal record," he said.

He called for the proposed law to be brought before a parliamentary select committee so that MPs could work towards legislation that was effective and enforceable.

1c9558d381626972: Every piece of AI content from Google's Gemini models has a hidden SynthID label, which makes it very difficult to pass the content off as authentic. SynthID has also gotten buy-in from other major AI players, but actually checking for those invisible watermarks has been a convoluted process. It's going to be a little easier going forward, though. Google has announced that its SynthID detector now supports watermarks from all its partners, and it's available for anyone to use on a new dedicated website.

SynthID is an invisible signal encoded in the pixels of AI-generated images and videos, and in the waveform of AI audio. Google says Gemini alone has integrated SynthID with over 180 billion images and videos, plus 240,000 years of audio. Until now, the only way for those outside of Google's trusted tester program to check for SynthID was to ask Gemini. This is rather clunky, and the model's output could sometimes be confusing when you just wanted a simple "yes" or "no."

Now you can cut Gemini out of the loop. Starting today, you can go to the new SynthID.com website to check a piece of content for an AI watermark. A major limitation of Google's previous detector was that it only checked for Google's version of SynthID. Even though ChatGPT images, for example, have SynthID, they wouldn't be flagged in Google's detector. That's no longer a problem.

445d70f6a3a1f061: BATU PAHAT: A two-year-old girl who was attacked by five stray dogs in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, last month has undergone three surgeries and will require several more procedures before she can be discharged from hospital.

Nur Haira Wafiqah is currently warded at the Paediatric Special Surgery Ward of Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA), Johor Baru, where she is under the close supervision of seven specialist doctors, her father said.
Mohammad Hamizi Hamdan, 37, said the first three surgeries involved treating and closing wounds on various parts of his daughter's body and head caused by the animal bites.
"The wounds on my daughter's legs, arms and body have started to heal, but the injuries to her head still require intensive treatment.
"This is Haira's fourth week receiving treatment at HSA and she is scheduled to undergo another surgery on her head this week," he said.
He said this when receiving a visit from a delegation of the Batu Pahat Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) Women's Association (Pelitawanis), at his home today.
Hamizi said the next series of surgeries would focus on tissue treatment, including the removal, repair and transplantation of damaged tissue.
The procedures will be carried out periodically and are expected to require Haira to remain in hospital for several more months.
"My wife, Nur Wahyuni Harun, 36, takes care of Haira at the hospital, while I travel back and forth from Batu Pahat to Johor Baru two to three times a week.

"After the first surgery, which took more than seven hours on the day of the incident, Haira only regained consciousness three days later. At first, she did not recognise anyone, but, Alhamdulillah, a few days later she began recognising me and her mother," he said.
He said Haira is now in stable condition, able to converse and eat normally.
However, doctors had informed the family that she could suffer permanent impairment, including impaired hair growth on several parts of her head.

Meanwhile, Batu Pahat TNB Pelitawanis chairman Datin Adib Nafilah Abu Dardak said the visit was to check on Haira's latest condition and present a contribution to help ease the family's financial burden.
In the 7am incident on Sept 5, Haira sustained serious injuries to almost her entire body after being attacked by a pack of stray dogs in front of her house.

Batu Pahat police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani had earlier confirmed that the victim was rushed to Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) in Batu Pahat for initial treatment before being transferred to HSA for specialist treatment.
cba9b694a2e9a8d1: For a while, I swore by Bissell’s Little Green carpet cleaner. I liked the sub-$100 price, the fact that it was small enough to fit on a closet shelf, and that it does a good job of cleaning up little messes. However, after you clean enough spots around the place, eventually the entire carpet needs a cleaning because the cleaned spots appear in stark contrast. It looks bad!

For a job that big, I upgraded (after doing a lot of research) to Bissell’s ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus. It’s a great upright machine with more power, though I wish I had waited, having paid $279.99 about a month ago. You can currently get one for $209.99 during October Prime Day at Amazon and Bissell (discount reflects at checkout).
Bissell ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus carpet cleaner
Bissell’s Little Green is handy, but doesn’t cut it for big jobs. If you have pets and a lot of carpet to clean, this is one of the most powerful upright carpet cleaners in its price range.

While the Little Green leaves the scrubbing up to you (it handles the sucking), the ProHeat 2X has plenty of deep-cleaning brushes, large reservoirs for dirty water and for cleaning fluid, plus an accessory port that lets you connect a brush-equipped hose for spot cleaning, essentially duplicating every feature I liked of the smaller model.

You’ll need to pony up for some cleaning solution after a handful of large-scale cleaning efforts, and it’s about $23 for a big bottle. I’ve found that you don’t need to use as much of the solution per gallon of water as Bissell notes on the bottle.
Unfortunately, one of my cats threw up at various places around our apartment last night (why can’t cats just do it all in one place?), so I’ll be using this carpet cleaner today. Wish me luck.

78323e4a4dc5db01: PETALING JAYA: Former Klang MP Charles Santiago has urged the government to include initiatives in the 2027 budget to upskill at least 1,000 Indian youths and reduce the school dropout rate in the community.
Santiago said the government should set a specific target of 1,000 Indian youths for upskilling, with candidates identified through schools, open applications, and NGOs.
He said the training could be delivered through technical and vocational education and training (TVET) and other programmes, with particular emphasis on cybersecurity and digital occupations.

Santiago also cautioned against framing the issue simply as a problem of “gangsterism” among Indians, saying this could unfairly stigmatise the community.
He said the government should set up a Cabinet committee on Indian affairs chaired by the prime minister.
“The committee would bring together senior ministers and secretaries-general of ministries to directly coordinate and accelerate policies affecting the Indian community,” he said.
Its immediate focus should be expanding skills training and addressing school dropouts.

In August, a coalition of 19 Indian NGOs known as Gelombang Saksama proposed establishing a dedicated statutory body, a public-private funding vehicle and a Cabinet committee to address the Indian community’s socio-economic challenges.

ccccc503e61b42e2: European mobile operators are gaining a slightly larger share of smartphone sales, not because they are selling more devices, but because other sales channels are shrinking faster. This is according to market watcher Counterpoint Research, which says that sales of new smartphones through European operators were down by 4 percent during the second quarter of this year, compared with the same period a year ago. But device sales through the open market fared much worse, declining by 11 percent. This refers to phones that are bought outright from independent retailers or directly from manufacturers, which are typically SIM-free and unlocked so the customer can choose which network they hook up to. Operators accounted for 36 percent of European smartphone sales in the second quarter, up from 35 percent a year earlier. The open market still represented the majority. As The Register has covered numerous times this year, mobile phones have been hit by the AI-driven memory crisis, which has led to a shortage of the DRAM and NAND flash components needed for consumer kit like smartphones and PCs. The resulting rise in prices has been felt most keenly at the lower end of the market, effectively making it commercially unviable to produce budget devices, according to some reports. Phones sold through operators tend to be higher-end models than those bought on the open market. Contracts spread the handset cost over monthly payments, making expensive devices more accessible. Apple played a key part in this slight shift, Counterpoint says, overtaking Samsung as the brand with the greatest market share in Europe's operator channel. Motorola and vivo are highlighted as the fastest-growing bands in the same segment. Counterpoint associate director Jan Stryjak said operators were likely to keep gaining market share for the next few quarters at least, as the lower end of the market continues to be impacted by the memory crisis. 0a185023e5a9d7aa: From Ng Sze Fung
Every year, Malaysia’s healthcare debate returns to the same question: how much more should the government spend? The 2027 budget will be no different.
There will be calls for more doctors, more nurses, better hospitals, newer equipment and higher allocations.
All of these are necessary and known. But throwing more money into the same administrative structure will only get us so far.
The harder question is more structural in nature.

Malaysia runs a highly centralised public healthcare system. That model has important strengths. National financing and common standards help prevent access to healthcare from depending entirely on where someone lives.

But centralisation also creates rigidity. The healthcare needs of Selangor, Penang, Kelantan, Sabah and Sarawak are not identical, yet staffing, service planning and resource decisions still operate largely through the same federal machinery.

The answer is not simply to create 13 separate health systems. Nor can healthcare simply be “handed over” to the states. The Federal Constitution is clear. Under the Ninth Schedule, medicine and health fall under the Federal List, while public health, sanitation and disease prevention sit partly within the Concurrent List.
Any serious proposal for decentralisation must therefore work within this constitutional structure, not pretend it does not exist.

Fortunately, decentralisation need not be equated with constitutional disruption. The federal government can continue to finance healthcare, set national standards, regulate professions and medicines, and redistribute resources between richer and poorer states.
At the same time, states or regional health authorities could be given greater discretion over how services are delivered locally.

That could mean more flexibility in workforce deployment, clinic and hospital planning, maintenance spending, primary care integration and partnerships with private providers where public capacity is stretched.
Local authorities could also play a larger role in preventive health, particularly where healthcare overlaps with sanitation, urban design and community wellbeing.

The guiding principle should be simple: centralise what protects equity, decentralise what benefits from local knowledge. The biggest risk is postcode healthcare, where richer states pull ahead while poorer states struggle.
That is why financing should remain largely federal, with allocations based on population need, age, disease burden, geography and deprivation.

Sarawak could provide a useful starting point. The state has already pushed for greater healthcare autonomy under the Malaysia Agreement 1963, including greater control over healthcare planning and the decentralisation of certain regulatory functions to the Sarawak health department, arguments shaped in part by the realities of delivering healthcare across a vast and dispersed population.
Rather than treating Sarawak as an exception, its experience could serve as a practical test of how greater local discretion can operate within a federally financed health system.
Malaysia needs to make its healthcare system less administratively rigid.

If the 2027 budget is serious about reform, the debate should not stop at how much more healthcare receives. It should also ask who is best placed to decide how that money is used, and perhaps the states are the best place to start that discussion in the spirit of decentralisation.
Ng Sze Fung is a senior analyst with Bait Al Amanah, a think tank.

98492ffd9a815b26: KUALA LUMPUR: National squash player Yasshmita Jadish Kumar sacrificed one year of her studies, and it led to her improving her world ranking by 27 rungs.
The 22-year-old from Negri Sembilan, who started the year at world No. 89, is now ranked 62nd.
She took a one-year break from her business management studies at Western London University in England to train in Cairo last October under coaches Andrew Shoukry and Ahmed Faragallah.
And Yasshmita has decided to take another one year break to continue training in Cairo.
She shone in her last two PSA World Tour events.

In the Nash Cup in Canada last month, Yasshmita reached her first PSA World Tour Copper-level final. Seeded ninth, she upset France's third seed and world No. 45 Lauren Baltayan in the second round for her first victory over a world top 50 player.
Yasshmita, whose parents are financing her squash activities, lost to Egypt's former world No. 7 Rowan Elaraby in the final.

She continued her momentum to win the Internazionali d'Italia Open title in Italy. Seeded third, she upset Italian top seed Cristina Tartarone in the semi-final, and in the final she beat Spain's Noa Romero.

Yasshmita said: "I am really happy with the way I have been playing over the last few tournaments. I started the year ranked 89th in the world, so to have moved up and getting closer to the top 50 is something I am very proud of.
"I know there is still a long way to go, and I don't want to put too much pressure on myself. My focus is to take it one tournament at a time, keep working hard and continue improving my game.
"Hopefully, by the end of the season in April 2027, I can get as close as possible to the top 50.

"I would also like to thank Matrix Concept for their continued trust, support and belief in me. Their support, especially during some of the more challenging periods of my journey, has meant a lot to me."
Yasshmita, currently playing in the qualifying rounds of the Egyptian Open in Cairo, will also feature in the Asian Team Championships in Islamabad, Pakistan from Nov 3-7.

3cd0976b38277f01: KUALA LUMPUR: Salutica Bhd has proposed a private placement of up to 30 per cent of its issued shares to raise up to RM16.18 million to fund its expansion into property development and construction.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the placement would involve up to 30 per cent of its issued shares, excluding treasury shares, to third-party investors to be identified later.
Based on an illustrative issue price of 11.5 sen per share, the exercise will raise gross proceeds of up to RM16.18 million.
The final issue price will be fixed later at a discount of not more than 20 per cent to the five-day volume-weighted average market price of Salutica shares immediately before the price-fixing date.

Of the proceeds, RM8 million will be allocated to expanding the proposed property development and construction business, while up to RM8 million will be used to expand its existing manufacturing operations.
Salutica said the proposed diversification would cover property development, construction and related activities.
This includes design-and-build works, trading and supplying construction materials, property management and property investment.
The company currently derives all of its revenue from manufacturing, which has been loss-making in recent financial years.
It recorded a net loss of RM23.75 million for the 12 months ended June 30, 2026, compared with RM29.76 million in the financial year ended June 30, 2025.
Salutica said the diversification would broaden its earnings base and reduce its reliance on manufacturing.
It is initially targeting smaller construction and property-related projects before taking on larger projects as it gains experience.
As at Sept 15, Salutica had not secured or entered into any construction, property development or property investment projects.
The proposed private placement and diversification are subject to shareholders' approval at an extraordinary general meeting.

“Langkah ini selaras dengan Deklarasi Geneva, Sumpah Hippocrates serta Deklarasi Alma-Ata 1978,” katanya ketika menggulung perbahasan Laporan Ketua Audit Negara mengenai kewangan KKM.

dfa7d7ca31bbad39: PABNA (Bangladesh), Oct 7 — Bangladesh is preparing to switch on its first nuclear power plant, a long-delayed project promising relief from chronic electricity shortages — even as some fear living beside it.

The 2.4-gigawatt Rooppur nuclear plant, a US$13-billion (RM53.1 billion) project more than a decade in the making, has transformed the once sleepy nearby village of the same name, bringing Russian workers, new businesses and jobs.

Once fully operational, its two reactors are expected to supply more than 10 per cent of electricity demand in the South Asian nation of 170 million people, which has been hit hard by the fuel crisis sparked by the conflict in the Middle East.

For Md Zahedul Hasan, managing director of state-owned Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh, the giant complex represents the culmination of a decades-old ambition to bring nuclear power to the country.

The plant’s first reactor is scheduled to be turned on by the end of this year, and the second unit “will be operational within a year”, Hasan said at the site on the banks of the Padma River, 150 kilometres (93 miles) west of Dhaka.
Bangladesh’s power sector is dominated by fossil fuels, particularly natural gas, with coal, oil and renewables making up the rest.
‘Changed me’
The project, built with Russian state nuclear corporation Rosatom, has also brought an unlikely Russian enclave to rural Bangladesh.
Thousands of Russian workers have spent years building and installing equipment, with a residential complex, shops and restaurants springing up around them.
Shop signs appear in Bangla, English and Russian, while some restaurants serve borscht soup alongside local dishes.
Alexander Vladimirovich Skvortsov, a Russian installation technician, said he had a choice between working in Turkey or Bangladesh. He chose Rooppur, moving there with his family in 2024.
“When I first saw the construction site at Rooppur, I realized how much work lay ahead on this project... honestly, Rooppur changed me and my life,” he told AFP.
The project has also transformed the local economy.
Md Emon Khan, 28, left his garment-factory job in Dhaka and returned to Rooppur, where he now sells vegetables and fruit to workers.
“I can speak a bit of Russian, and they can speak Bangla, too,” he said.
Plant officials say stringent safety measures have been followed and lessons from previous nuclear accidents were incorporated into the project.
Standing near a radiation monitoring tower and an alarm post, 15-year-old Mohammad Nafiz said he saw little to fear.
“We are glad that Rooppur is known to the world, and my friends and I hope that we will work at the plant after graduating from engineering schools,” he added.
Not everyone shares that confidence.
Md Yunus Ali, 80, whose home is a 15-minute walk from the plant, said opposition to building a nuclear facility in the densely populated area dates back decades.
“A few days ago, they ran a compressor test with a big bang... even the children who were asleep woke up in fear,” said Ali, a retired paper mill worker.
“I am old now, and I am not afraid for my life... but I have children and grandchildren, and I want safety for them.”
‘Full benefit’
The ambition to build a nuclear power plant at Rooppur dates back to the 1960s.
Several attempts came after independence, including approaches to Saudi Arabia and France, and talks with China and South Korea. No deals materialised.
Bangladesh finally signed an agreement with Moscow in 2015, with the Russian state offering a loan covering about 90 per cent of the project’s original cost.
Construction began in 2017.
The project has since faced delays, including disruption from the Covid-19 pandemic and sanctions on Russia after its invasion of Ukraine, which complicated equipment deliveries and payments.
There have also been corruption allegations surrounding the project, including against ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and members of her family. They have rejected the accusations.
For most Bangladeshis, however, the biggest question is when Rooppur will finally deliver reliable electricity.
Belly Begum, a 55-year-old farmer, struggles to irrigate her land during frequent power cuts.
“I wish the Rooppur nuclear power plant goes into operation soon, and we reap the full benefit,” she said.
“I hope we will get electricity for 24 hours without interruption, as the plant is near my house.” — AFP
2e55e2dc72b86cc4: OSLO, Oct 7 — Donald Trump’s chances of winning the Nobel Peace Prize are seen as minimal, but his “spectre” will cast its shadow over Friday’s announcement of the winner in Oslo, experts say.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee knows it will be under close scrutiny: since his return to the White House in January 2025, the billionaire Republican has campaigned intensively for the prize and hasn’t hidden his disappointment at not winning it yet.

The chances of him getting the nod are however undermined by his war against Iran, his territorial ambitions — sometimes at the expense of allies, as in Greenland — and his attacks on international cooperation institutions and the media.

Even though he has not been lobbying as openly for the Nobel in recent weeks, Trump remains on everyone’s minds, with strong chances that the committee’s pick will, regardless of who they choose, be interpreted as direct or indirect criticism of the US president.
Trump is “the spectre in the room”, said the head of the Peace Research Institute in Oslo (PRIO), Haakon Gjerlow.
He said the Nobel committee must be asking itself: “Is there any potential for this prize to create harm rather than good in awarding it?”, given the reactions that could emerge from the White House.
The Nobel Institute says it is unfazed.

“There’s always a lot of lobbying, and ultimately perhaps also attempts to exert pressure on the committee. So in one sense we’re very used to that,” the secretary of the committee, Kristian Berg Harpviken, told AFP.
“It’s not something we don’t discuss. Of course we have to discuss it, but it’s not like that influences the discussions in the room and decisions that come out,” he insisted.
‘Age of predators’
Last year, the prestigious prize went to Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, a choice generally considered palatable to Trump.
Machado even gave him her Nobel gold medal, judging he deserved it after the capture of President Nicolas Maduro — though she failed to obtain his political backing in exchange.
Those events could prompt the committee to this year choose a laureate who enjoys broad consensus, such as an individual or organisation working to protect children or humanitarian efforts.

That could include the Save the Children charity and Mykola Kuleba, a Ukrainian children’s rights activist campaigning for the return of kids illegally taken to Russia from occupied territories — a cause close to the heart of Trump’s wife Melania.
Sudan’s Emergency Response Rooms (ERR), a vast network of volunteers risking their lives to help people facing the double threat of war and hunger, could also be a potential laureate.
But the committee may also choose a laureate that could rub Trump the wrong way.

That could include the UN special rapporteur for the occupied Palestinian territories Francesca Albanese, Pope Leo XIV, press freedoms with an award to the Committee to Protect Journalists, or international justice bodies such as the International Criminal Court (ICC) and the International Court of Justice (ICJ).
“We live in an age of predators. We have Trump, Putin, Netanyahu,” said Nobel historian Asle Sveen.
“They don’t want to have an international order. They want to have big powers with spheres of influence. And this court stands in the way,” he said, referring to the ICC.
A total of 287 individuals and organisations have been nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize, though the names on the list are kept secret for 50 years.
But peace remains elusive in many parts of the world: 65 armed conflicts involving at least one state actor were registered in 2025, the highest number since 1946, according to PRIO.
“At an overall level, it is clear that the world is not developing in the right direction,” said Harpviken.
“At the same time... there is no lack of good initiatives. There is no lack of organisations or individuals who do good work,” he said.
“A peace prize may make more sense than ever.” — AFP
0b6e591d564929d8: WARSAW, Oct 7 — Assassinated Russian reporter Anna Politkovskaya, shot dead outside her Moscow home in 2006, had “predicted” Russia’s trajectory under Vladimir Putin, her editor told AFP ahead of the 20th anniversary of her death.
Politkovskaya had reported fearlessly on the war in Chechnya and the rise of Putin, warning of his authoritarian tendencies at a time when he was being welcomed and courted in the West.
She was gunned down in the lift of her central Moscow apartment block on October 7, 2006 — Putin’s 54th birthday.
Her killing marked a turning point for Russian journalism.

Two decades on, Putin is still in power, Moscow’s war against Ukraine — which has killed hundreds of thousands — is in its fifth year, and domestic repression has reached levels not seen since the Soviet era.

“Everything that is happening with Russia was predicted by Anna Politkovskaya in the books she published before her death,” Sergei Sokolov, the legendary reporter’s editor at the Novaya Gazeta newspaper where she worked, said.
Moscow has labelled her paper, Novaya Gazeta, a “foreign agent”.
“At the time, nobody believed her and they said she was exaggerating the dangers and fears,” Sokolov said.

As the West embraced Putin in the early 2000s — a strongman leader cautiously welcomed after the chaos of the previous decade — Politkovskaya warned Russian journalists would have to show “total servility to Putin” or face death or prison.
Russia, she said, was “hurling back into a Soviet abyss.”
The gunmen behind her murder are in prison — but the person, or people, who ordered the killing have never been named.
Asked about that in 2021, Putin said his agencies “did everything to uncover these crimes”.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Journalist Sergei Sokolov attends a gathering in memory of the slain Russian reporter Anna Politkovskaya at the office of the Novaya Gazeta newspaper, recently designated by authorities as a ‘foreign agent’, in Moscow October 6, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Nothing could make her stray’
In death, Politkovskaya has become an even more totemic figure for Russian journalists — inspiring a generation of investigative reporters who she never met, and who are now forced to work in exile.
With Russia at war in Ukraine, her reporting from both sides of the frontline in the Chechen wars has taken on fresh relevance.
She covered war crimes committed by both the Russian army and Chechen rebels and pushed both to evacuate civilians.
In 2002, she walked into a Moscow theatre that had been seized by Chechen rebels to try to secure the release of hostages.
“The terrorists had chosen me as a person they wanted to talk to, I couldn’t refuse,” she later said.
More than 130 hostages would be killed when special forces gassed the theatre and stormed the building.
“What stood out in her was her tenacity — nothing could make her stray from the topic or idea she had,” Sokolov, her editor, recalled.
That school of journalism now lies in virtual tatters.
Years of pressure from the Kremlin has culminated in censorship levels unseen since the Soviet Union.
If Politkovskaya were alive, Sokolov was certain: “she would definitely not be able to stay silent”.
In her later years, Politkovskaya had become a fierce critic of Ramzan Kadyrov, then being groomed as the future head of Chechnya.
She dubbed him a “little dragon” and accused him of being given a free hand to brutally rule over the war-torn region in exchange for loyalty to the Kremlin.
Kadyrov in turn called her an “enemy of the Chechen people”, vowing she would “answer” for her criticism of him.

Dmitry Muratov (left), a Nobel Prize-winner, one of the founders of the Novaya Gazeta daily, and journalist Sergei Sokolov (centre) attend a gathering in memory of the slain Russian reporter Anna Politkovskaya at the office of the Novaya Gazeta newspaper, recently designated by authorities as a ‘foreign agent’, in Moscow October 6, 2026. — AFP pic
Icon

Despite her name being virtually erased in Russia’s official narrative, Politkovskaya remains an icon for independent Russian journalists — but also a constant reminder of the dangers of her profession.

“You need an example. If there was no example of courageous journalists and if everyone kept their heads down, then things will be even worse for Russian journalism,” 28-year-old exiled reporter Yegor Feoktistov said.
“Her fate always reminds you of what can happen — but it also gives you courage.”
Another investigative journalist forced to work in exile, Olga Churakova, said she is “surprised by the stream of people who want to become journalists” in Russia despite the dangers.
Many mention Politkovskaya as their inspiration.
“People still come and say: ‘Someone needs to do this job’.” — AFP
344a8e5911cbabd5: ISTANBUL, Oct 7 — Three years into Israel’s genocide in the Gaza Strip, Palestinian and UN data show sweeping consequences for women and girls, from deaths, injuries and disappearances to rising miscarriage rates, unsafe births and malnutrition, Anadolu Ajansi reported.

The collapse of Gaza’s health system has also deprived pregnant women of medical care, forcing some to give birth at home or in displacement shelters, while changes in family structures have left tens of thousands of women responsible for supporting their households.
Data released by the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics on July 18, 2026, showed that 12,400 women, excluding girls, had been killed in Gaza since October 7, 2023.

The bureau also said women and children accounted for 4,700 of the 11,200 people reported missing, with the fate of many still unknown amid fears that some remain under the rubble of destroyed buildings.

UN Women, in an April 2026 report titled The Cost of War on Women and Girls, estimated that more than 38,000 women and girls were killed between October 2023 and December 2025 — an average of nearly 47 per day.
The report added, “there are close to 11,000 women and girls with lifelong injury.”
Survivors continue to face daily risks from bombardment, hunger, repeated displacement and restrictions on access to essential services, the report said.
According to the report, more than 71,200 Palestinians were killed during the period it covered, with women, children and older persons together representing more than half of all fatalities.
It cautioned that the figure was likely lower than the actual death toll “given the collapse of health information and reporting systems.”
The highest proportion of deaths among women and children was recorded during the first six months of the war, when they accounted for nearly two-thirds of documented fatalities.

The report said that despite a ceasefire agreement that took effect on October 10, 2025, women and girls continued to be killed and injured, while humanitarian and health conditions threatening their lives showed no significant improvement.

From the early months of the genocide, rights and health organisations documented a sharp deterioration in women’s reproductive health amid attacks on medical facilities, lack of access to health care, repeated displacement and malnutrition.
In July 2024, the International Planned Parenthood Federation said miscarriages in Gaza had risen by at least 300 per cent during the first nine months of the war.
Physicians for Human Rights said in January 2026 that its report, Destroying Hope for the Future: Reproductive Violence in Gaza, documented 2,600 miscarriages during the first half of 2025.
The report also documented 220 pregnancy-related deaths and 1,460 premature births, while more than 2,500 newborns required intensive care.
Earlier data from Gaza’s Health Ministry showed that 57.1 per cent of registered pregnant women in 2025 suffered from anemia.
Rights reports said pregnant women in Gaza faced growing difficulty obtaining prenatal and delivery care as the health system deteriorated.
UN Women said Gaza was recording about 130 births per day as of March 2025, with more than a quarter delivered by cesarean section, placing additional strain on an already weakened health system.
The collapse of health services forced many women to give birth at home and in displacement sites, away from emergency medical care, the report said.
Even after the ceasefire, around 15 births per week continued to take place outside hospitals, often without skilled midwives and in unsafe conditions.
Hunger and malnutrition also heightened risks for pregnant women and newborns, including low birth weight, premature delivery, stillbirths and maternal deaths.
By July 2025, 40 per cent of pregnant and breastfeeding women in Gaza were suffering from malnutrition, while around half a million women and girls faced the risk of famine, according to UN Women.
The report estimated that 37,000 pregnant and breastfeeding women, along with 50,000 girls, would require treatment for acute malnutrition during the year following the ceasefire.

In another report issued on June 19, 2026, UN Women said 1 million women and girls in Gaza lacked access to clean water, 690,000 were living in overcrowded shelters and 328,000 girls were out of school.
The latest figures from Gaza’s Health Ministry show that risks facing pregnant women continue despite the ceasefire.
The ministry recorded around 3,958 miscarriages between January and June 2026.

An infographic published by the ministry on July 20 showed the miscarriage rate reached 208.5 per 1,000 live births during the first half of 2026, compared with 64 per 1,000 live births in the second half of 2025 — about 3.3 times the previous rate.
April recorded the highest monthly miscarriage rate at 377.25 per 1,000 live births, while June recorded the highest number of miscarriages at 790.

The data show that 73.6 per cent of miscarriages occurred during the first trimester, before the completion of 13 weeks of pregnancy, while 26.4 per cent occurred during the second trimester, between 13 and 24 weeks.

The war has also reshaped thousands of families in Gaza, forcing more women to assume responsibility for supporting their households following the deaths, injuries or disappearance of their husbands and the loss of income.
According to UN Women, the proportion of Palestinian households in Gaza headed by women rose from nine per cent before the war to 14 per cent.
The report said 58,600 households were now headed by women as a result of the war.

It said the shift has placed long-term economic and social burdens on women and girls, alongside caregiving responsibilities and protection needs stemming from displacement, poverty and the loss of family members.
Israel continues to violate the ceasefire that took effect on October 10, 2025, with 1,460 Palestinians killed and 5,116 injured in attacks through Monday, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.

Since the genocide began in October 2023, more than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed and over 175,000 injured, while around 90 per cent of Gaza’s infrastructure has been damaged or destroyed. — Bernama-Anadolu

88534e319a9cd5e2: KYIV: Ukraine's agriculture minister on Wednesday said his country would not agree to EU membership if that would entail permanent restrictions on farm subsidies and exports of agricultural products.
The response comes a day after the European Commission proposed a special arrangement that would limit financial support and restrict exports, such as wheat, from Ukraine.
"Transitional periods are a normal part of EU enlargement... Permanent restrictions on access to the single market are an entirely different matter," Taras Vysotsky said in a statement to AFP.
"Ukraine cannot agree to such an approach."
The government in Kyiv had not yet received any official proposal, which is due to be discussed by EU leaders at a summit next week, he added.
The proposal was aimed at alleviating worries of current EU member states, some of which fear newcomers would backslide on democracy or hoover up too many key resources.
Ukraine, which is a major exporter of corn, wheat, colza, sunflower seeds and vegetable oil, submitted its EU membership bid days after Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.
It was granted official candidate status a few months later, with accession negotiations kicking off in 2024.

But the prospect of the agricultural powerhouse joining one day has sparked fears in countries such as France and Poland that it would sap the EU's vast programme of farm subsidies and flood the market with cheaper produce.

Vysotsky said Ukrainians "understand the sensitivity of certain segments for European farmers" and were open to "substantive discussions about adaptation periods, the scale of market access and safeguard mechanisms".
But he rejected permanent restrictions, which he said "would contradict the very logic of full membership in the EU".

64e1bc2b104e67d0: KUALA LUMPUR: More than 80 per cent of outstanding medical bills involving non-citizen patients involved undocumented migrants and stateless people.

"The amount fell from an estimated RM359 million in 2024 to RM336 million in 2025, a reduction of RM23 million or 6.4 per cent," she said.

Hanifah said outstanding medical bills involving non-citizens were caused not only by weaknesses in the collection process, but also by patients' limited financial capacity and lack of insurance coverage.
Among other factors, she said, were patients leaving healthcare facilities without settling their bills, and incomplete or inaccurate identity and contact information.
She said these factors made it difficult for the ministry to trace patients and follow up on outstanding payments.

To address the issue, she said Health Ministry healthcare facilities had taken several collection measures, including issuing three reminder letters, serving legal notices, contacting patients' embassies or next of kin, and making claims against employers.
"The ministry also worked with non-governmental organisations to help patients settle their bills if they were unable or had limited means to pay," she said.
f8275288c4965935: KUALA LUMPUR: The health ministry has proposed making health insurance coverage or contributions compulsory for registered refugees and asylum seekers to help cover their treatment costs and prevent new medical bill arrears.

Hanifah said the ministry’s overall accounts receivable fell from RM359 million in 2024 to RM336 million in 2025, a drop of 6.4%.
She said unpaid medical bills involving non-citizens were not solely caused by weaknesses in fee collection.
They were also linked to patients’ financial constraints, lack of insurance coverage, patients leaving health facilities without paying, and incomplete or inaccurate identity and contact information.
“These make it difficult for the health ministry to trace patients and take follow-up action for collection purposes," she said.

She said public health facilities had taken several steps to recover the money, including issuing three reminder letters at intervals, sending legal demands or notices, contacting patients’ embassies or next of kin, seeking payment from employers, and working with NGOs to help settle bills owed by those unable to pay.

The ministry was also strengthening its “collect before discharge” approach by mandating deposits and payments during treatment, expanding cashless payment options, and stepping up monitoring of accounts receivable.

c4023de2e32fd044: GENEVA: More than 200,000 people have been displaced from their homes since fighting in Yemen began in recent weeks, according to data released on Wednesday by the UN's International Organization for Migration.

The Houthis, who already control most of northern Yemen, including the capital Sanaa, seized the country's entire Red Sea coast last month from Saudi-backed forces of the internationally ​recognised government, based in the southern port of Aden.
People have been displaced across 10 governorates, with Ta'iz the hardest hit.
More than 3,700 people have also fled by sea to Djibouti, IOM said.
On Friday the UN World Food Programme said that three in four ​families in parts of Yemen were going hungry from the "absolutely devastating" impact of a surge in fighting.

a71241c71650f77c: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association has urged swift action to address critical healthcare manpower shortages in Sabah and Sarawak, welcoming proposals by Senator Dr R.A. Lingeshwaran to strengthen the workforce in both states.
MMA president Dr L. Sivanaesan said many of the measures were consistent with solutions MMA had previously mooted, but these must now be backed by funding and a firm implementation timeline.
"The solutions are already on the table. What is needed now is the political will, adequate funding and a firm implementation timeline.

"Hospitals operating with only a handful of medical officers cannot afford to wait for another committee, another review or another announcement that the matter is being looked into," he told the New Straits Times.
Dr Sivanaesan warned that every delay adds burden on remaining personnel and risks further weakening healthcare delivery in both states.
"The time for studying the problem is over. Sabah and Sarawak need decisive action now, not more promises," he said.

He said MMA had raised the concerns directly with the Health Ministry's top leadership and urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in his capacity as finance minister, to ensure sufficient funding in the 2027 Budget to address the shortages.
MMA had also called on the Sabah and Sarawak governments to consider supplementary incentives for healthcare personnel, including special allowances, housing and other support.
"Resolving this crisis will require a concerted effort by both the Federal and state governments."
Dr Sivanaesan said the government must take a comprehensive approach, as short-term fixes or isolated incentives would not be enough.

Beyond financial incentives, healthcare workers needed manageable workloads, fair on-call arrangements, protected rest, access to leave, safe and suitable accommodation, and clear pathways for transfers, postgraduate training and career progression.
He said the measures must extend beyond doctors to include other healthcare professionals.

Earlier, Lingeshwaran had proposed 11 immediate measures to make postings in Sabah and Sarawak fairer, more attractive and sustainable, including a standard 24-month service period after which doctors with satisfactory performance could apply for transfers, specialist training or their next placement.

The Parliamentary Special Select Committee on Health has also called for a review of existing allowances and incentives, with committee member Young Syefura Othman saying some hospitals were operating with as few as three medical officers.
a74462e061596e10: NEW YORK: The interest rate on the most common US home loan jumped last week to its highest in almost three years, worsening affordability for buyers four weeks before elections that will decide if President Donald Trump's Republicans keep control of Congress.
The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage surged 19 basis points to 7.49 per cent in the week ended October 2, the Mortgage Bankers Association said on Wednesday. It was last higher in November 2023.

Mortgage rates are closely tied to the yield on US 10-year Treasury notes, which earlier this week hit a 24-year high, driven by concerns over inflationary pressures from soaring oil prices and data showing stronger US economic growth.

The cost of living is the top issue on Americans' minds as they decide how they will vote on November 3, a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday showed, and is one reason why Trump's approval rating is at a record low of 32 per cent.

Home borrowing rates are up about 1.4 percentage points since joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran began in late February, tracking a similar rise in the 10-year Treasury yield, which topped 5.3 per cent on Monday.
Inflation is also on the rise, registering 3.4 per cent in August by a measure that the Federal Reserve targets at 2 per cent.

Federal Reserve policymakers have signalled they expect to follow their September interest-rate increase with another rate hike by year's end, though markets are for now betting they will not move at their upcoming policy meeting at the end of October.
Mortgage loan applications fell 4.2 per cent last week from the previous week, the MBA said on Wednesday, with refinancing applications dropping sharply.

"Very few homeowners have an incentive to refinance at these rates, and the jump in borrowing costs has caused many potential borrowers to step back from the purchase market," said Joel Kan, the MBA's deputy chief economist.
692847b450437176: Nine out of ten respondents to a survey of VMware customers say higher licensing costs were prompting them to consider alternatives. Unisphere Research surveyed 269 executives, managers, and professionals at VMware user organizations between December 2025 and February 2026. The study, commissioned by third-party support provider Rimini Street, also found that 54 percent cited the end of perpetual license support as a reason to evaluate other options. The study showed cost remains the leading driver of virtualization roadmap decisions. Seventy-three percent said savings were a top priority. Respondents also identified barriers to change: operational complexity (40 percent), multi-vendor management challenges (38 percent), securing the increased attack surface (37 percent), and team skills requirements (37 percent). Users were looking for choice, flexibility, and control over their virtualization strategies, said Keith Costello, chief operating officer with Rimini Street, which sells third-party support for VMware. "These survey findings reinforce the need for practical, vendor-independent strategies that put business priorities back on the client's terms." Sixty percent of respondents were considering a multi-hypervisor strategy. Forty-eight percent said they did not currently plan to move any assets to VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF), Broadcom's subscription platform and preferred migration path. Broadcom agreed to buy VMware in 2022. By November 2024, Gartner was arguing that customers were worse off because of the acquisition. In May 2025, cloud customer group the European Cloud Competition Observatory (ECCO) and cloud trade association CISPE claimed that Broadcom had upped VMware licensing costs to between eight and 15 times their previous levels since it acquired VMware. At the time, Broadcom said it was working to advance the European Union's sovereign cloud objectives and enable enterprises to "accelerate innovation, provide more choice, and address their most complex technology challenges." In June, UK retail giant Tesco said it was replacing VMware with an alternative product and pressing ahead with its licensing lawsuit against the virtualization pioneer's parent company, Broadcom, with a High Court trial scheduled no earlier than November 2027. Last month, Gartner predicted that more than half of enterprises would begin proofs of concept for alternatives to their VMware deployments by 2029, while still rating the Broadcom business unit a leader in two major markets. "By 2029, 55 percent of enterprises will initiate proofs of concept for alternative distributed hybrid infrastructure products to replace their VMware-based deployments and embrace hybrid cloud infrastructure delivery, up from 25 percent in 2026," it said. ®
92d4ce491b76d076: BARCELONA: Spanish World Cup winner and former Barcelona winger Pedro Rodriguez retired from football on Wednesday at the age of 39.
The forward won the 2010 World Cup with Spain as well as three Champions League titles with Barca, two of those in 2009 and 2011 as part of Pep Guardiola's team which dominated that era of the sport.
Pedro also won five La Liga titles with the Catalan giants, was a Premier League winner at Chelsea, before heading to Roma and finally Lazio.
"I feel that the moment has come. The moment to take a step forward and begin a new stage in my life," said Pedro in a post on social media.
"I leave proud of having lived my dream and of all the people who were by my side to make it come true."
Born in Tenerife, Pedro joined Barcelona's youth academy as a teenager and made his first-team debut in 2008.
Under Guardiola, he became a key figure in the side that won an unprecedented six trophies in 2009.

Pedro netted in the 2011 Champions League final win over Manchester United and scored 99 goals for Barcelona in 321 games, playing with Lionel Messi, Andres Iniesta and Xavi Hernandez among other stars.
"Being part of the best Barca side in history was a privilege, we won everything and amazed the world," said Pedro in his farewell video.
As well as lifting Spain's first World Cup trophy Pedro also won the 2012 European Championship with La Roja.
"One day, almost without believing it, I became a world champion and a starter in a World Cup final," said Pedro, who earned 65 caps and scored 17 goals for his country.
Arriving in 2015 at Chelsea, he won the Premier League in 2017, as well as the FA Cup and Europa League in the subsequent two seasons.
Pedro's final club was Lazio, whom he left at the end of last season after more than 200 appearances for the Serie A side.
14ef819d7261a698: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 7 — The Regent of Johor Tunku Mahkota Ismail has decreed for all schools in the state to close following the persistent haze and unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings,” said Johor Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali.
He explained that the two-day closure, starting tomorrow and the following day, was due to the ongoing haze compounded with a deteriorating air quality across all districts in the state.
“The closure affects 617,258 students across 1,198 schools that comes under the administration of the Education Ministry.
"All schools throughout Johor will be closed on October 8 and 9 as a precautionary measure to safeguard the student’s safety and health,” he said in a statement issued today.
Dr Muhammad Naqib pointed out that for schools involved in the Year 4 Learning Matrix (MPT4) or any other assessments, the implementation will be postponed and rescheduled.
He said this will be subjected to directives from the Johor Education Department (JPNJ) and relevant authorities.

“During the two-day closure period, Teaching and Learning at Home (PdPR) sessions will be conducted to ensure the learning process continues,” he said, adding that the state government and relevant agencies will continue to monitor API readings regularly.
Dr Muhammad Naqib said the state government understands that such a decision may impact parents and guardians who still need to work.
Therefore, he said the granting of appropriate work flexibility to affected parents or guardians by their employers will be greatly appreciated.
“I also urge parents to continue monitoring their children's health, ensure they stay hydrated and limit any outdoor activities.
“Parents or guardians need to seek immediate medical attention if their children experience coughing, sore throat or shortness of breath," he said.
Earlier, Johor recorded unhealthy API readings, with figures between 161 and 197, from eight monitoring stations.
Batu Pahat was the worst hit with an API reading of 197 in the morning.
Yesterday a total of 335 education institutions in the Batu Pahat district were ordered to close after the API reading in the district reached 208 last night.
5f62e3170d1877ff: KUALA LUMPUR: The Finance Ministry (MoF) rejected three proposals to commercialise or take over the e-Jamin system last year, opting instead to retain the existing arrangement at no cost to the government, the Dewan Rakyat was told.

Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said the decision was made on Oct 22, 2025, after Dapat Vista Malaysia Sdn Bhd had proposed three options to resolve issues surrounding the system operated by itself.

He said the options were for the government to purchase the e-Jamin system directly from Dapat Vista, subscribe to its services and products, or retain the company to maintain and operate the system before eventually handing it over to the government.
"The final decision by the MoF on Oct 22, 2025 was to reject all three commercial proposals.

"MoF decided to maintain the existing system at no cost to the government through an official agreement, together with a trustee bank structure," he said when winding up the debate on the Auditor General's Report in the Dewan Rakyat.

The three proposals included a model under which Dapat Vista would maintain and operate the system for five years before handing it over to the government, at an estimated overall cost of RM80 million.
Kulasegaran said the government recognised concerns over the absence of a formal agreement governing the system, which has been in operation since 2020.
He said e-Jamin was initially introduced as a "stop-gap measure", but had continued to operate for a prolonged period because of the difficulties that arose when the system was previously stopped.

"When the company suddenly ceased operations, there was total chaos among lawyers throughout the country, which created difficulties for us to continue because the old system was very troublesome and required this system to continue," he said.
He said this, however, was not a justification for the absence of a formal contract.
"There is no excuse for not signing a contract so that the terms are more open, with accountability and transparency," he said.
Kulasegaran said the matter was being scrutinised by the relevant departments and was expected to be brought to the cabinet soon for its consideration and views.
He said the government also acknowledged the need to ensure that the funds handled through the system were properly protected.

"The more important thing is that I agree that we need to expedite the agreement so that the terms can be known by the people and there is accountability, and all parties can know about the matter," he said.

The e-Jamin system enables bail payments to be made electronically, with the government saying it reduces the time needed to complete bail payments to less than 30 minutes compared with about five hours under the previous physical payment process.
Kulasegaran said 81,667 bail cases were recorded through the system in 2025, involving RM255.198 million in bail money.
He added that based on the audit information available, there had been no misappropriation of the funds.
The PAC had previously raised concerns over the management of bail money under e-Jamin, including the absence of a formal government contract and the investment of part of the funds by Dapat Vista.
c608b9b61009ed78: MOSCOW, Oct 7 — The Kremlin today appeared to reject reports of a second suspected plague case in Siberia, telling reporters when asked about the accounts that most media reporting on the situation was “false”.

The United States, the European Union and the World Health Organisation have all called on Russia to be transparent over the reported plague death of a laboratory technician at a plague research institute in Siberia’s Irkutsk region last week.
WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus also called today for Moscow to clarify “media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause”.
Asked about the reports, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters that “the media reports a great deal”.

“And the vast majority of what the media is reporting regarding this situation is false information,” he insisted, calling on people to rely solely on official statements from Russia’s health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor.
Peskov also said he had “no information” regarding a formal request from Washington for clarifications about the situation.
A source close to the matter had said yesterday that the United States had made such a request via a confidential diplomatic communication, known as a demarche.
Russian news outlet People of Baikal reported Friday that the dead woman — named as 28-year-old Darya Shipilova — may have contracted pneumonic plague from a broken test tube.
Other media reported a possible link between her death and a lab accident at the facility.
The People of Baikal outlet also said up to 200 people with whom she may have had contact were under quarantine.
But Russian authorities say the cause of death is not confirmed and Rospotrebnadzor has denied claims circulating in a document online that special measures have been put in place. — AFP
1c2945e35339f86a: PETALING JAYA: A minimum wage hike risks increasing operating costs in the construction sector, which could in turn drive up property prices and project costs, the Master Builders Association Malaysia (MBAM) said today.

Its president, Kenneth Liew, said the cost of labour was among the largest components in the construction industry, making any increase in the minimum wage likely to affect employers’ operating costs.
Liew said the construction sector’s heavy reliance on foreign workers meant the additional cost would not be limited to basic wages but would also involve overtime rates and related payments.

“Many contractors are tied to fixed-price contracts signed before this review and cannot easily pass on the additional costs to buyers. If the burden is not shared, it will eventually be reflected in project costs and property prices,” he told FMT.

To ease the pressure, he said, the government should implement the minimum wage hike in stages through consultations with the industry, while providing a price adjustment mechanism for existing public and private sector contracts.

Persatuan Kontraktor Bumiputera Kelas F Malaysia president Tukiman Radion said most small contractors were not directly affected by the wage structure adjustment as a large proportion of their workers were freelancers or family members.
However, he said, a minimum wage hike would put pressure on some contractors who employed permanent workers for maintenance and cleaning duties.
“Projects handled by small contractors are mostly small-scale and are still based on old prices.
“Permanent workers start asking for higher wages when the minimum wage is raised, while the payments contractors receive from customers remain the same,” he said.

On Aug 18, human resources minister R Ramanan said the government was reviewing the RM1,700 minimum wage, with the decision on whether to maintain or raise the rate to be made by the National Wages and Gig Economy Consultative Council.
Details on whether the rate will be increased are expected to be announced during the tabling of the 2027 budget on Oct 9.
Entrepreneur development and cooperatives minister Steven Sim has confirmed that micro, small and medium-sized enterprises would be exempted from further increases in minimum wage for the time being.
ec85fa6a22246bc8: KUALA LUMPUR: Crude palm oil (CPO) prices could return to the RM5,000-per-tonne level as early as in the first quarter (Q1) of 2027, driven by potential disruptions to the sunflower oil market and developments surrounding the Russia-Ukraine conflict, said an analyst.

ISTA Mielke GmbH executive director Thomas Mielke said CPO prices could also potentially regain the US$1,300-per-tonne level for free-on-board (FOB) palm oil prices, but the timing remained uncertain.

"We can easily get RM5,000 (CPO prices) back again, and US$1,300 back again for Malaysian FOB palm oil. The question is when. I would assume we will see this back again as early as January," he said in a panel discussion at the Malaysian Palm Oil Forum (MPOF) Kuala Lumpur 2026 here today.

The session was moderated by Cable News Network (CNN) anchor and correspondent Eleni Giokos. Also on the panel were Glenauk Economics managing director Dr Julian McGill and Frost & Sullivan chemicals material and nutrition director Nikhil Vallabhan.
Mielke said the developments surrounding the Black Sea sunflower oil corridor could also provide support to palm oil prices.

He said global palm oil annual production growth is likely to ease to 1.3 million tonnes or less in the 10 years to 2030 from an average of annual growth of 2.9 million tonnes in the 10 years to 2020.
"However, palm oil is still dominating the global market of oils/fats with a production share of 31 per cent and export share of 49 per cent this year.
"The commodity no longer needs to gain market share via price discounts, except for relatively short periods of temporary oversupply," he added.
86d71a6ae533cff9: KUALA LUMPUR: Defence minister Khaled Nordin has taken a swipe at Lumut Naval Shipyard Sdn Bhd (Lunas), which is owned by the finance ministry, over the prolonged delay to the littoral combat ship (LCS) project.
Khaled maintained that the defence ministry was the customer or client in the LCS project, not the contractor tasked with building and delivering the vessels.
He said he hoped Lunas would not give any more excuses or delay the completion of the project beyond the current expected delivery date of April 2027.
"As the purchaser, the defence ministry is definitely hoping that the LCS vessels will be delivered (to us).

"If the new date is April 2027, we hope Lunas will not delay further or give any more excuses," he said when winding up the ministry's debate on the Auditor-General's Report on the LCS project in the Dewan Rakyat today.
"I believe that, with the cooperation and commitment of the finance ministry, Lunas will not delay the delivery any further and hand over the ships to the defence ministry in April 2027.
"I believe the finance ministry will also take steps to preserve its good name, since Lunas is owned by the ministry.”
Khaled said the delay had affected the military's defence preparedness.
The A-G's report released on Monday said the LCS 1 could be handed over without complete training and weapon systems, and might not be fully operational until December 2035.
It found that trials and commissioning could not be completed on schedule, with five complementary contracts for weapons and support systems still incomplete.
The audit also found that, as of June 25, the overall LCS project was 7.55% behind schedule across all five ships, with delays ranging from 30 to 108 days.

The LCS project, which had an original cost of RM9 billion, is said to be the largest defence procurement in Malaysia’s history. Due to delays and cost overruns, the cost ballooned to RM11.22 billion while the number of vessels to be delivered was reduced from six to five.
1225ebcf0f297240: SINGAPORE: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has warned that global economies face three major crosscurrents with the rapid arrival of artificial intelligence (AI), persistently high energy prices, and record levels of public debt.
IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva said the global economy is also being pulled in two opposite directions -- a negative energy supply shock and a positive demand shock from AI.
She said higher energy prices are pushing up inflation, policy rates and benchmark yield curves.
"This takes us to the third major factor affecting the global economy today: excessive fiscal deficits, record levels of public debt and high debt-servicing costs.

"Global public debt is nearing its highest levels since the end of World War II and is on track to exceed 100 per cent of global gross domestic product (GDP)," she said in a presentation entitled "Outlook for The Global Economy and Policy Priorities" on Wednesday.

The speech was made at the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy in Singapore ahead of the 2026 IMF Annual Meeting in Thailand next week. Also present at the event was Singapore President Tharman Shanmugaratnam.
Meanwhile, Georgieva said the IMF estimated that AI hardware and related technology products now account for more than one-tenth of world goods trade and are rising.
"Love it, hate it, or fear it, AI is here, rapidly becoming a key driver of countries' relative fortunes in the world economy.

"Global investment-to-GDP in AI will reach and likely exceed the amounts that went into building the railroads, the electricity grid, or the telecommunication network," she said, adding that growth in AI-related trade reflects the investment boom in economies embedded in its value chain.
She also noted that IMF research suggests that AI, if done right, could over time deliver up to half a percentage point of extra world growth annually.
"Just think of it going from 3.0 per cent to 3.5 per cent -- it will add an economy the size of Asean to the world economy over a decade.
"We will learn as we go, but we know AI preparedness is key, including digital infrastructure, labour market readiness, and regulatory guardrails," she added.

Popular weight-loss drugs may do more than help people shed pounds. They might also slow the aging process.
Drugmakers Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk say patients taking their GLP-1 drugs age less quickly, according to molecular “aging clocks” that track changes in DNA or levels of key proteins.

10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch: Energy Dome and its carbon dioxide batteries
Energy Dome is one of MIT Technology Review’s10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch 2026, available exclusively to subscribers.

Solar and wind are among the cheapest and quickest ways to add electricity to the grid. But they’re subject to variations in weather patterns, so supplies can be intermittent. Energy Dome has an unusual solution: massive batteries that use compressed carbon dioxide to store energy for when the grid needs it.

Compressing gas to store energy isn’t new. Utilities have used compressed air in underground caverns to hang on to reserves for decades. But Energy Dome’s approach doesn’t require any specific geology to work, so it could be more easily scaled to help grids around the world.
Here’s how the company is using carbon dioxide to store renewable energy.

MIT Technology Review Narrated: Don’t be fooled—LLMs don’t reason
—Thore Graepel, a core member of DeepMind’s AlphaGo team

Ten years ago, I watched a program I helped build stun the world by beating Go champion Lee Sedol. AlphaGo won after making a move so strange that some commentators thought it was a programming glitch. It was AlphaGo’s powers of reasoning that made this creative choice—and these are powers that today’s AI lacks.
This is why I recently left my position at Google DeepMind. I believe we need a fresh approach to machine reasoning, one that draws on AlphaGo’s architecture.

6bf8ec2f317ff1cf: PETALING JAYA: Kenaikan gaji minimum berisiko meningkatkan kos operasi sektor pembinaan, yang seterusnya boleh menaikkan harga hartanah dan kos projek, kata Persatuan Kontraktor Binaan Malaysia (MBAM).

Presiden Kenneth Liew Kiam Woon berkata, kos buruh merupakan antara komponen terbesar dalam industri pembinaan, sekali gus menjadikan sebarang peningkatan gaji minimum memberi kesan kepada kos operasi majikan.
Menurutnya, pergantungan tinggi sektor pembinaan kepada pekerja asing menyebabkan beban kos tidak hanya terhad kepada gaji asas, malah melibatkan kadar kerja lebih masa (OT) dan bayaran berkaitan.
"Banyak kontraktor terikat dengan kontrak harga tetap yang ditandatangani sebelum semakan ini dan tidak boleh memindahkan kos tersebut dengan mudah kepada pembeli.
"Jika beban ini tidak dikongsi, ia akhirnya akan muncul dalam kos projek dan harga hartanah," katanya kepada FMT.

Bagi mengurangkan tekanan, Liew menggesa kerajaan melaksanakan kenaikan gaji minimum secara berfasa menerusi konsultasi bersama industri, di samping menyediakan mekanisme penyelarasan harga bagi kontrak awam dan swasta yang sedia ada.

Sementara itu, Presiden Persatuan Kontraktor Bumiputera Kelas F Malaysia, Tukiman Radion, menerangkan kebanyakan kontraktor kecil tidak terjejas secara langsung dengan pelarasan struktur gaji kerana sebahagian besar pekerja mereka terdiri daripada pekerja bebas atau ahli keluarga.
Namun kenaikan gaji minimum memberi tekanan kepada sesetengah kontraktor yang memiliki pekerja tetap bagi tugas penyelenggaraan dan pembersihan, katanya.
"Projek yang dikendalikan kontraktor kecil kebanyakannya berskala kecil dan masih berasaskan harga lama.
"Pekerja tetap mula meminta gaji lebih tinggi apabila gaji minimum dinaikkan, sedangkan bayaran yang diterima kontraktor daripada pelanggan masih kekal sama," katanya.

Pada 18 Ogos lalu, Menteri Sumber Manusia, R Ramanan, berkata kerajaan sedang menyemak semula kadar gaji minimum RM1,700, dengan keputusan untuk mengekalkan atau menaikkan kadar itu akan dibuat Majlis Perundingan Gaji dan Gig Negara.
Perincian sama ada ia akan dinaikkan dijangka diumumkan semasa pembentangan Belanjawan 2027 pada 9 Okt ini.

Bagaimanapun, Menteri Pembangunan Usahawan dan Koperasi Steven Sim Chee Keong mengesahkan perusahaan mikro, kecil dan sederhana (PMKS) dikecualikan daripada kenaikan tersebut buat masa ini bagi mengelakkan tekanan kos operasi.

09588e84d314572a: SHAH ALAM: Mahkamah Tinggi memerintahkan seorang penunggang motosikal yang hilang upaya kekal dalam kemalangan di lebuh raya pada hari terakhir 2018 mendapat ganti rugi RM1.17 juta selepas mendapati pemandu kereta yang terlibat bertanggungjawab sepenuhnya atas kejadian itu.
Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman Shoba Dorai Rajah mengetepikan pembahagian liabiliti 70-30 oleh Mahkamah Sesyen yang meletakkan kesalahan sebanyak 70% atas penunggang berkenaan, S Thenesh.
Berdasarkan penilaian Mahkamah Sesyen, Thenesh menerima ganti rugi RM400,000.
Shoba berkata, kerosakan terhadap dua kenderaan berkenaan selain keterangan saksi dan bukti lain menunjukkan bahawa pemandu, Norba’idah Abd Majid tiba-tiba memasuki laluan Thenesh.
“Bukti fizikal kerosakan berkenaan sangat muktamad,” katanya dalam penghakiman bertulisnya.
Katanya, kereta Norba’idah hanya mengalami kerosakan pada kiri bampar belakang manakala motosikal Thenesh rosak di kanan ‘fork’ depannya.
Beliau berkata, ini tidak konsisten dengan dakwaan defendan bahawa Thenesh melanggar bahagian belakang kereta itu.
“Bukti forensik menyokong keterangan plaintif mengenai kejadian itu apabila defendan pertama tiba-tiba memasuki laluan kiri untuk ke jalan susur,” katanya.
Shoba turut menerima keterangan saksi, S Jayachitra yang sebelum ini ditolak Mahkamah Sesyen.

Katanya, keterangan Jayachitra disokong kerosakan terhadap kenderaan, susun atur jalan dan pengakuan Norba’idah sendiri bahawa dia menuju ke Taman Kota Cheras melalui jalan susur ketika kejadian pada 31 Dis 2018 itu.
Katanya, Mahkamah Sesyen turut terkhilaf apabila bergantung pada andaian bahawa Norba’idah mungkin membrek secara tiba-tiba, sedangkan Thenesh mendakwa sebaliknya.

Shoba turut menolak hujah bahawa amnesia retrogred dialami Thenesh menyebabkan kesnya tidak dapat dibuktikan, sebaliknya memutuskan liabiliti boleh dibuktikan menerusi saksi bebas, pengakuan, serta bukti fizikal dan dokumen.

Mahkamah turut mempertimbangkan bahawa Norba’idah dikenakan kompaun trafik sebanyak RM300 kerana menukar laluan secara salah. Katanya, walaupun ini bukan bukti konklusif terhadap liabiliti, ia tetap menunjukkan pemanduan yang tidak bertimbang rasa.
Thenesh hilang upaya kekal dan tidak lagi dapat bekerja akibat kecederaan otak, retak pelbagai tulang di mukanya selain hampir hilang sepenuhnya deria pendengaran pada telinga kanan.
Mahkamah Tinggi membenarkan rayuannya atas liabiliti, menolak rayuan defendan dan memerintahkan kos RM10,000 untuk setiap rayuan.
Thenesh diwakili peguam Jagjit Singh dan Premjit Singh, manakala C Manimaran dan S Nirmala mewakili Norba’idah dan Hazlishahmi Mohamad iaitu pemilik berdaftar kereta berkenaan.
Kedua-dua pihak telah memfailkan rayuan di Mahkamah Rayuan.
c22b9fdde3ae8afc: MOSCOW: The Kremlin on Wednesday appeared to reject reports of a second suspected plague case in Siberia, telling reporters when asked about the accounts that most media reporting on the situation was "false".
The US, the EU and the WHO have all called on Russia to be transparent over the reported plague death of a laboratory technician at a plague research institute in Siberia's Irkutsk region last week.
WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus also called Wednesday for Moscow to clarify "media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause".
Asked about the reports, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters that "the media reports a great deal".

"And the vast majority of what the media is reporting regarding this situation is false information," he insisted, calling on people to rely solely on official statements from Russia's health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor.
Peskov also said he had "no information" regarding a formal request from Washington for clarifications about the situation.
A source close to the matter had said on Tuesday that the US had made such a request via a confidential diplomatic communication, known as a 'demarche'.
Russian news outlet People of Baikal reported Friday that the dead woman – named as 28-year-old Darya Shipilova – may have contracted pneumonic plague from a broken test tube.
Other media reported a possible link between her death and a lab accident at the facility.
The People of Baikal outlet also said up to 200 people with whom she may have had contact were under quarantine.
But Russian authorities say the cause of death is not confirmed, and Rospotrebnadzor has denied claims circulating in a document online that special measures have been put in place.
